sales.summary:
Time, Team, Capacity and Tracks are four thin admin surfaces sitting on a much richer schema than any of them render, plus one client-facing tracks story that lives in two different, inconsistent places.

TIME (`/time`, admin-only, feature key `time`) is a single flat list of `time_entries` with two view tabs (Entries table / By client accordion), three summary tiles, three charts, a FilterBar (billable / client / team member), a search box, a date-range picker, an "Export CSV" button and a "Log time" slide-over. The live timer is NOT on this page at all: it lives in the top-nav `TimerChip` (start/pause/resume/stop/discard, three-source picker over Requests | Tasks | Clients plus a "None, general" row, 30s heartbeat, stale-timer recovery dialog) and in the per-request/per-task `TimeCard`. The page fetches one unparameterised page of 50 rows and does every filter client-side, while the summary tiles report the unbounded totals, so the "Entries" number and the table routinely disagree. The rate-loss issue is real and confirmed: the Log-time form has a "Rate ($/hr)" input, the client sends `hourlyRate`, and `POST /api/admin/time` neither reads nor inserts it, even though `time_entries.hourly_rate` exists and is the only thing the Xero export and the monthly billing email price from. `taskId`, `startedAt`, `endedAt` and `source` are likewise present in the schema and invisible on this page.

TEAM (`/team`, admin-only, feature key `team`) has a Members table (DataTable, 7 columns, one Role filter chip, search) and an Org chart tab. Row actions: Edit, Send login invite (only when unlinked), Manage access, View as, Remove. Two slide-overs share one `MemberForm` (name, email, title, role, skills, weekly capacity, contractor). The Access panel writes the OLD `team_member_access` table (access role project_manager/task_handler/viewer, client scope all_clients/plan_type/specific_clients, track type all/small/large) which is a different system from the newer `/permissions` builder. Deny-by-default is genuinely enforced in `lib/access-scoping.ts` + `lib/access-scope.ts`, but the panel's `trackType` and two of its three access roles are inert, and the panel's defaults hand out `all_clients` on first Save.

CAPACITY (`/capacity`, admin-only, feature key `capacity`) is four KPI cells, a utilisation bar, a Pipeline Capacity Impact block (weighted/worst/best case + a per-month deal table), an 8-week Recharts line chart, a per-member capacity bar list, and a Sales Call Helper with a deal-impact calculator. Its "Committed hours" comes from a hardcoded two-entry `PLAN_HOURS` map (`maintain: 8, scale: 16`), not from logged time, so every other plan contributes zero; the 8-week timeline is three flat lines by construction; the per-member bars show capacity share, never utilisation. Real per-member utilisation from actual time entries already exists at `/api/admin/reports/utilization` (used by `/reports`) and `/api/admin/pipeline/capacity` (used by the owner home) — neither is wired into `/capacity`.

TRACKS is split. The `/tracks` page is client-facing but is NOT in `CLIENT_NAV`, so no client can reach it; an admin who opens it gets an explainer empty state. The mini-kanban component (`TrackQueueView`, lanes Up next / In progress / Review / Delivered, drag-reorder, ghost upsell cards, priority-bump confirm) is used in three places on two different API stacks: `/tracks` and the admin client-detail Track tab read `/api/{portal,admin}/capacity`, while the actual live client surface, the Overview "Your work in motion" `TrackBoard`, reads `/api/portal/tracks` with a different, buggier bucketing rule. `tracks.current_request_id` is never written by any route, so every track's "In progress"/current slot is permanently empty; and the admin client-detail Track tab renders `TrackQueueView` with no `onReorder`, so an admin's drag reorders optimistically and silently reverts.

THE RATE LOSS, CONFIRMED: time-list.tsx:135 sends `hourlyRate: hourlyRate ? parseFloat(hourlyRate) : undefined`. app/api/admin/time/route.ts:133-141 declares the body type WITHOUT hourlyRate, and the insert at app/api/admin/time/route.ts:165-176 writes id, orgId, requestId, teamMemberId, hours, billable, notes, date, createdAt, updatedAt — no hourlyRate. The column exists: db/schema.ts:822 `hourlyRate: real('hourly_rate')`. Every rate typed on /time is silently discarded.

RATE LOSS DOWNSTREAM 1: app/api/admin/billing/xero-export/route.ts:73-98 groups billable entries by org using `entry.hourlyRate`, falls back to `organisations.defaultHourlyRate`, and `continue`s (skips the client entirely) when the resolved rate is 0. Because /time never stores a rate, every hourly client without a defaultHourlyRate is silently skipped from the draft-invoice run.

RATE LOSS DOWNSTREAM 2: app/api/admin/billing/monthly-email/route.ts:72 computes `existing.amount += entry.hours * (entry.hourlyRate ?? 0)` with NO org-default fallback, so the monthly billing summary emails $0.00 for every client. It is hardcoded to send to ['liam@tahi.studio'] (monthly-email/route.ts:144) while the operator account is business@tahi.studio.

Accepts orgId, teamMemberId (incl. the literal 'me'), billable ('0'|'1'), dateFrom, dateTo, page. limit is HARDCODED 50 (route.ts:26). Applies scopedOrgIds and returns an all-zero empty payload on scope 'none' (route.ts:29-34). Returns items[] with { id, orgId, orgName, requestId, requestTitle, teamMemberId, teamMemberName, hours, billable, notes, date, createdAt } (route.ts:80-93), ordered by date desc, plus { page, limit, totalHours, billableHours, entryCount, capacityHours }. hourlyRate, taskId, startedAt, endedAt and source are never returned.

DraggableItem is still draggable and doMove still mutates local state (components/tahi/track-queue-view.tsx:459-483), but `onReorder?.(...)` at line 480 is a no-op, so the new order vanishes on the next SWR revalidation. Studio-side, a client can reorder their own queue and Tahi cannot.

/api/portal/tracks duplicates every request across same-type tracks. app/api/portal/tracks/route.ts:80-83 builds each track's queue by filtering the org's whole request list on type, with no per-track assignment and no dedup across tracks. A maintain+priority client with two small tracks sees the identical queue twice on the Overview, and because queueOrder is a single global column, reordering 'Track 1' visibly reorders 'Track 2' too.

/api/portal/tracks drops any request that is not exactly 'small_task' or 'large_task'. The same filter at route.ts:82 is an equality test on the LEGACY requests.type column, whose comment (db/schema.ts:428-430) says it has been replaced by `size`. Requests typed bug_fix, content_update, consultation or anything an intake form produces appear in no lane on the client Overview board. The /tracks + client-detail stack uses trackCanHandle instead (lib/track-lanes.ts:63-64), which places them, so the two client-facing views of the same queue disagree.

/tracks is unreachable for the audience it was built for. lib/feature-tree.ts:64 declares it appliesTo ['client'], but CLIENT_NAV (components/tahi/nav-model.tsx:122-146) has no entry for it and no page links to it. A client can only land there by typing the URL; an admin who does gets the 'Manage tracks from a client' explainer. Two full mini-kanban stacks (this one on /api/portal/capacity, the Overview TrackBoard on /api/portal/tracks) exist for one job.

/capacity's 'Committed (Subscriptions)' is invented. app/api/admin/capacity/start-date/route.ts:19-22 hardcodes PLAN_HOURS = { maintain: 8, scale: 16 }. Every other plan type the product sells (tune, launch, hourly, custom, and any org with tracksMode custom) contributes 0. No logged time, no track load and no estimatedHours ever feed this number, yet it drives the Utilization %, the Available figure, the utilisation bar, all three Pipeline Impact tiles, the timeline chart and the Sales Call Helper.

/capacity's 8-week timeline is three flat lines. capacity-content.tsx:122-138 pushes the SAME { total, committed, forecasted } triple for i = 0..7. The chart titled 'Capacity Timeline (next 8 weeks)' cannot slope, because start-date returns one constant and no future subscription or deal dates are consulted.

'Earliest start' can only ever be next Monday or never. app/api/admin/capacity/start-date/route.ts:84-92 loops 12 weeks but the loop condition (availableHoursPerWeek >= estimatedHoursPerWeek) is invariant, so it either breaks on week 0 (earliestDate = next Monday, weeksOut = 1) or falls through to null. The '(N weeks out)' hint at capacity-content.tsx:424 always says '1 week', and the code comment at route.ts:68-69 admits it.

/capacity's per-member bars are not utilisation. capacity-content.tsx:361 computes width as `(cap / totalCapacity) * teamMembers.length * 100`, i.e. each member's share of the AVERAGE. Everyone on the same weekly capacity renders a full bar. Under a heading 'Team Member Capacity', beside a page-level 'Utilization' KPI, this reads as workload and is not. Real per-member utilisation already exists at /api/admin/reports/utilization and /api/admin/pipeline/capacity and is not used here.
Dead code in the capacity page: CapacityKPI + ACCENT_COLORS (capacity-content.tsx:442-467) are fully defined and never rendered; the file uses KPIStrip/KPICell instead.

/api/admin/capacity/start-date and /forecast have no feature gate. Both check isTahiAdmin only (start-date/route.ts:25-28, forecast/route.ts:11-14), unlike GET /api/admin/capacity which calls requireFeature('capacity') (route.ts:24). A team member denied the Capacity feature is redirected off the page and loses the nav item, but can still read total team capacity, every open deal's title, NZD value and close probability straight from the endpoints. Same shape at /api/admin/team/org-chart (route.ts:9-12), which returns full teamMembers rows including clerkUserId while GET /api/admin/team carefully downgrades that same data to a LITE projection for feature-denied callers.

The two MCP get_capacity paths are broken. app/api/mcp/route.ts:254 and mcp-server/index.ts:220,328 fetch /api/admin/capacity with no ?orgId=, which that route answers with 400 'orgId required' (app/api/admin/capacity/route.ts:28). (mcp-server/ is the dormant local server per feedback_mcp_worker_only, but the in-app /api/mcp route is not.)

The Access panel's 'Track type' select does nothing. app/api/admin/team/[id]/access/route.ts:125 persists it, the GET reads it back, /permissions copies it — and lib/access-scoping.ts never reads it. 'Small only' and 'Large only' change no query anywhere in the codebase.

Two of the three 'Access role' options do nothing. Only 'project_manager' is ever consulted, and only for notification recipients (lib/notify-request-team.ts:101, app/api/portal/calls/route.ts:285) and client PM assignment (app/api/admin/clients/[id]/pm/route.ts:41,84,104). 'task_handler' and 'viewer' have no readers, so choosing between them changes nothing about what the person can see or do.

The Access panel violates deny-by-default on first save. team-content.tsx:549-553 initialises the form to role 'task_handler', scopeType 'all_clients'. Opening it for a member with no rules shows the correct warning ('This member cannot see any client data') and then, if the admin presses 'Save access' without touching anything, grants them every client. The safest scope is not the default.

The Access panel silently destroys multi-rule configurations. It hydrates from rules[0] only (team-content.tsx:566-574) while the PUT deletes ALL of the member's teamMemberAccess rows and inserts exactly one (app/api/admin/team/[id]/access/route.ts:94-128). Any member given several rules (e.g. via /api/admin/permissions/copy-access, which loops and inserts one row per source rule) loses everything but the first the next time someone opens and saves this panel.

The Team page has two contradictory definitions of 'linked'. The banner uses email matching (`m.email === user.primaryEmailAddress`, team-content.tsx:788-791) while the Login column uses clerkUserId (team-content.tsx:1011-1019). A member whose email matches but whose clerkUserId is null makes the info banner disappear while the warning banner and a 'Not linked' badge stay up.

'Manage access' is offered to people the API will refuse. The row action is unconditional (team-content.tsx:1303) but the PUT is gated by requireFeature('settings.permissions') (access/route.ts:64). A team member who can see /team but not the permissions surface fills the whole form and gets a bare 'Forbidden' on Save. 'Remove' has the same shape against requireManagePermissions.

'View as' changes nothing on the surfaces being mapped. setTeamMemberImpersonation writes sessionStorage and clears the org cookie (components/tahi/impersonation-banner.tsx:128-138); only the sidebar, the mobile nav, the clients list and the requests list read impersonatedAccessRules. /time, /capacity, /tracks and /team itself continue to fetch and render everything, so the banner claims a scoped view the page is not honouring.

The org chart cannot be built from the UI. Its empty state says 'Add reporting relationships to your team members to build the org chart' (components/tahi/org-chart.tsx:538), but reportsToId and department are only settable through PUT /api/admin/team/[id] (route.ts:72-73) and appear in no form: MemberForm (team-content.tsx:113-256) has no reports-to or department field. The only way to create a non-flat tree today is to hang a Planned Role off someone, and even that form omits the reportsToId the route accepts (org-chart.tsx:342-350 vs planned-roles/route.ts:36,54).

Clicking a member in the org chart goes nowhere. components/tahi/org-chart.tsx:527-529 pushes `/team?member=${memberId}`, and team-content.tsx never reads useSearchParams or a 'member' param. The click just re-renders /team on the Members tab with nothing selected.

Team cost data exists in the database and is used by nothing. hourly_cost_rate, compensation_type and annual_salary were added to team_members by migration 0016 (app/api/admin/db/migrate/route.ts:133-135) and are deliberately kept out of the Drizzle schema (db/schema.ts:193-195). Repo-wide grep finds no other reference. Without a cost rate there is no margin on any time entry, which is the gap behind /capacity having nothing but headcount hours to show.

Deleting a team member leaves orphaned foreign keys. app/api/admin/team/[id]/route.ts:122-132 removes access rows then the member, but time_entries.team_member_id (db/schema.ts:820) and requests.assignee_id (db/schema.ts:443) both reference teamMembers.id with no ON DELETE behaviour and no pre-check. D1 does not enforce these, so the rows survive pointing at nothing and render as 'Unknown' on /time forever.

The monthly billing email is hardcoded to the wrong recipient and prices everything at zero. app/api/admin/billing/monthly-email/route.ts:144 sends to ['liam@tahi.studio'] (the operator account is business@tahi.studio) and line 72 multiplies hours by `entry.hourlyRate ?? 0` with no organisations.defaultHourlyRate fallback, unlike the Xero export at xero-export/route.ts:97. Given the /time rate loss, every row reads $0.00.

The Xero export has no idempotency and no plan filter. app/api/admin/billing/xero-export/route.ts:55-68 selects every billable entry in the month for every org regardless of billingModel or plan type, and lines 113-134 insert a fresh local invoice each run with no check for an existing invoice for that org+month. Running it twice bills a client twice; running it at all bills retainer clients for hours already covered by their plan.

track_lanes silently swallows work with no eligible track. lib/track-lanes.ts:76-80 and 96-99 `return` / `continue` when eligibleTrackId is null, so on a client whose tracksMode is 'custom' with zero counts, or whose plan grants no tracks (anything but maintain/scale, per lib/plan-utils.ts:41-48), every request disappears from the board with no message. The /tracks empty state only fires when tracks.length === 0 AND ghosts.length === 0.

sales.summary: Proposals, Contracts and Schedules are three sibling "sales artifact" surfaces built on the same spine: an admin builder shell (sticky toolbar + centre editor + right rail navigator), a token-minted public `/p/<type>/<token>` viewer, an admin-only `/preview/<type>/<id>` render of live unpublished state, a template system, Resend email delivery, and shared `share_view_events` / `share_section_views` analytics. Proposals and Schedules use a draft/publish snapshot model (public viewer reads `publishedSnapshot`, falls back to live); Contracts have no publish step (body is live and locks on signature). All three are admin-only in-app: `app/(dashboard)/{proposals,contracts,schedules}/page.tsx` hard-redirect a client to `/requests`, and `lib/permissions.test.ts:409-428` pins them out of CLIENT_NAV, so the only client-facing surface is the emailed token link plus the portal overview's ProjectBoard (derived from the shared schedule snapshot via `/api/portal/project`). Contracts and Schedules share the extracted `components/tahi/builder/index.tsx` primitives; Proposals still carries its own duplicated local copies of the same components. The delivery spine (#148) is real and one-directional: gantt rows are linked to requests/tasks (`requests.scheduleRowId` / `tasks.scheduleRowId`), `lib/delivery-status.ts` derives 6 statuses per row and rolls them up, surfaced in the admin gantt + EngagementHealthCard + off-track cron — but never in the public schedule viewer. Significant dead ends: the client-detail Contracts tab is typed against the retired legacy `contracts` table so its Download and Expiry columns are permanently broken; contract "Save as template" is wired to an endpoint that ignores `fromContractId` and 400s; contract template `{{variables}}` are never substituted because no create form collects values; the per-slide `data.theme` read by every proposal section renderer is never written by any editor; template snapshots silently drop `themeMode` on both proposals and schedules; and the analytics heatmap labels sections by aggregation order, not slide order.

Exhaustive map of the Leads, Calls and Deals surfaces for a redesign. Three sales surfaces sit in the sidebar "Sales" group (nav-model.tsx:58-71) alongside Proposals/Schedules/Contracts/Calculator/Sales analytics/Affiliates. All three are admin-only (orgId === NEXT_PUBLIC_TAHI_ORG_ID) plus a granular feature gate (`leads`, `calls`, `deals`, child `deals.engagement_health`).

LEADS is a two-headed surface: a DataTable list with a quick-view SlideOver (leads-content.tsx, 2183 lines) AND a separate full-page detail (leads/[id]/lead-page-content.tsx, 1416 lines). The two do not agree on fields: the slide-over edits source/sourceDetail/estimatedValue/currency; the full page edits 10 firmographic fields (industry, employees, revenue band, monthly visits, lead type, LinkedIn x2, country, year founded, tech stack, CMS) that the slide-over cannot see. AI is the centre of gravity: enrich (Sonnet + web_search + an in-house tech-stack sniffer), score (Haiku, daily cron + manual rescore-all), a 3-block briefing (snapshot/fit/watch-outs), company signals with per-claim source links, 3 lead-specific discovery questions + an always-ask template from settings, one-click "apply suggested fields", and an AI first-reply drafter with send-via-Resend.

CALLS is the thinnest surface (386 lines, one DataTable, 4 columns, 2 tabs, 1 filter). It reads a unified `discovery_calls` index but has NO detail page, NO row click, and no way to read a transcript even though it renders a "Transcript" badge. The real call UI is `<DiscoveryCallsCard>` (components/tahi/discovery-calls.tsx, 1152 lines), a polymorphic card embedded on lead, deal, request, task and org surfaces, which owns scheduling, post-call fields, AI transcript extraction and action-item→task creation.

DEALS is the heaviest: a kanban board with drag-drop + a paginated list view (deals-content.tsx, 2004 lines), a 5-KPI strip, and a 3496-line detail page with a stage progress rail, activity timeline (20 typed event kinds), notes, associated requests, a sales kit (proposal/schedule/contract quick-create), engagement health rollup, and a 14-section sidebar.

On an existing row the update set (sync-calendar/route.ts:295-306) writes title, scheduledAt, durationMinutes, googleMeetUrl, attendees and meetingType — but NOT leadId / dealId / orgId, which are only assigned at insert (:328-330). A call that synced before its lead existed stays 'Unlinked — triage' permanently, even after the lead is created with the matching attendee email.

THE /calls PAGE HAS NO DETAIL VIEW AND NO WAY TO READ A TRANSCRIPT. There is no app/(dashboard)/calls/[id]/ route, no onRowClick, and no renderExpand on the DataTable (calls-content.tsx:319-382). The table renders a positive 'Transcript' badge (:193-198) that links to nothing. The only way to read or edit a transcript is to navigate to the call's parent lead/deal/client and expand the row inside <DiscoveryCallsCard>. A transcript on an UNLINKED call is unreachable through the UI entirely.

/calls SILENTLY HIDES ANYTHING OUTSIDE ±60 DAYS. calls/index/route.ts:46-51 defaults since/until to now ±60 days. The page never passes ?since or ?until and offers no date filter, so the 'Past' tab quietly stops at 60 days back and 'Upcoming' at 60 days out. The tab counts (calls-content.tsx:296-301) present the truncated set as the whole set.

THE calls/index DOC-COMMENT LIES. It claims to read 'both discovery_calls ... and the legacy scheduled_calls (org-only check-ins)' (calls/index/route.ts:4-7), but the implementation only queries schema.discoveryCalls. Every scheduled_calls row created from the client-detail page (clients/[id]/client-detail.tsx:3670) or via the MCP create_call tool is invisible on /calls. Two parallel call tables, one surfaced.

THE `outcome` COLUMN IS FETCHED AND NEVER SHOWN ON /calls. calls/index/route.ts:69 selects it and calls-content.tsx:33 types it, but no column, badge or filter uses it. The same is true of `isClassified` (route :113) and `googleCalendarEventId` (:36).

DRIVE TRANSCRIPT SYNC HAS NO UI TRIGGER. /api/admin/integrations/google/sync-drive-transcripts is only reachable from the cron (`7,37 * * * *`) and the MCP tool drive_sync_gemini_transcripts. The /calls 'Sync calendar' button only hits sync-calendar (calls-content.tsx:97), so a user who wants transcripts now has no button to press.

THE TRANSCRIPT CHARACTER CAP IS MISSTATED. The textarea placeholder says 'Capped at 50k characters' (discovery-calls.tsx:934) but the server caps at TRANSCRIPT_MAX_CHARS = 250_000 (discovery-calls/[id]/route.ts:30) and the extractor only reads MAX_TRANSCRIPT_CHARS = 40_000 (extract/route.ts:27). Three different numbers, none of them shown correctly.

LEAD SOURCES AND DEAL SOURCES ARE DISJOINT, AND PROMOTE COPIES ACROSS THE GAP. promote/route.ts:187 sets `source: lead.source ?? 'lead'`. Lead sources include manual, webflow, email, affiliate, event, cold_outreach (leads-content.tsx:153-163); the deal source filter and label map know none of those except a 'cold_outreach' label alias (deals-content.tsx:188-200, 552-562). A promoted lead therefore shows a raw unstyled string on the deal card and can never be found by the /deals Source filter. The default fallback 'lead' is not in any list either.

PROMOTE IGNORES THE DEFAULT-OWNER SETTING. deals POST honours `pipeline.defaultDealOwnerId` (deals/route.ts:212-231), but promote resolves owner as lead.ownerId → the caller's own team-member row and stops (promote/route.ts:158-167). A lead with no owner promoted by a non-team-member caller (webhook, MCP) creates an unassigned deal even when the default-owner setting is configured. Likewise, POST /api/admin/leads uses a DIFFERENT setting key, `leads.defaultLeadOwnerId` (leads/route.ts:168) — two separate default-owner settings for one stated preference.

CLOSING A DEAL FROM THE STAGE DROPDOWN SKIPS THE WON/LOST CAPTURE. DealCloseDialog only fires on kanban drag-drop (deals-content.tsx:744-754). Choosing 'Closed Won' or 'Closed Lost' from the deal-detail StageSelector (deal-detail.tsx:1195-1212) PATCHes stageId alone, so wonSource and lostReason are never captured, no `won`/`lost` activity is written (those are gated on body.status, deals/[id]/route.ts:726-746), and the deal drops out of close-reason reporting. The list view has no stage control at all, so it cannot close a deal either.

ARCHIVED DEALS ARE UNREACHABLE. DELETE soft-deletes by setting closeReason = 'archived' (deals/[id]/route.ts:789-797) and GET /api/admin/deals hard-excludes them (:48). No filter, tab or query param surfaces them, and the deal detail's own fetch does not exclude them but nothing links there any more. The `unarchived` activity type exists (deal-detail.tsx:164, deals/[id]/route.ts:749-757) but no UI can ever trigger it.

THE DEALS BOARD IS SILENTLY CAPPED AT 100 DEALS. deals-content.tsx:223 requests ?limit=100 and the API clamps limit to 100 (deals/route.ts:30). There is no pagination on the board and no 'showing 100 of N' notice, and every KPI in the strip is computed from the truncated `filtered` array (:315). Past 100 deals the pipeline totals are simply wrong with no warning. The owner-home card documents this exact hazard and works around it (owner-home.tsx:949-951) — the /deals page does not.

THE OWNER HOME AND /deals CAN DISAGREE ON THE WEIGHTED NUMBER. /deals weights via effectiveProbability, which prefers historicalProbability over the static one (lib/pipeline-math.ts:187-189); /api/admin/reports/pipeline-forecast weights with the static stage.probability only (pipeline-forecast/route.ts, weightedU/weightedM). Same deals, two different 'weighted forecast' figures on two screens.

THE PIPELINE FORECAST IS NOT ACCESS-SCOPED AND IS GATED ON THE WRONG FEATURE. pipeline-forecast/route.ts:39 calls requireFeature(..., 'sales_analytics') and never calls scopedOrgIds, unlike GET /api/admin/deals. So (a) a team member with `deals` but not `sales_analytics` gets a 403 and the owner-home 'Pipeline ahead' card sticks on its shimmer forever, since loading = !dealsData || !forecast (owner-home.tsx:945); and (b) a member scoped to a subset of clients sees whole-pipeline money on their home page.

THE TWO LEAD SURFACES EDIT DIFFERENT FIELDS AND NEITHER IS COMPLETE. The slide-over LeadForm (leads-content.tsx:912-1045) is the only place to edit source, sourceDetail, estimatedValue and currency. The full-page editor (lead-page-content.tsx:963-1006) is the only place to edit industry, employeeCount, revenueBand, monthlyVisits, leadType, linkedinUrl, linkedinPersonalUrl, country, yearFounded, techStack and cms. Neither surface can edit affiliateCode or archiveReason at all, so archive activities (leads/[id]/route.ts:235-246) always land without a reason.

THE FULL-PAGE LEAD DRAFT CARRIES ownerId AND status BUT NEVER SENDS THEM. LeadDraft declares both (lead-page-content.tsx:107-108) and toDraft populates both (:163-164), but the saveEdit PATCH body (:299-324) omits them. They are dead fields on the form object; the hero quick-pickers are the only writers.

THE RE-ENRICH PROMPT CANNOT FIRE FROM THE LIST ROW ACTION. The trigger requires selectedLead.enrichedAt (leads-content.tsx:343), but the row-action `startEdit(r)` (:729, :293-298) seeds selectedLead from the LIST row, and GET /api/admin/leads does not return enrichedAt (leads/route.ts:57-80 selects only aiScore of the AI columns). Editing a website from the row action therefore never prompts a re-enrich; only editing from a slide-over that was opened via openLead does.

`?lead=<id>` ON /leads IS AN ORPHAN. leads-content.tsx:200-222 implements a deep-link that opens the slide-over in edit mode, with a comment saying it exists so 'the full-page detail's Edit button (which routes here with ?lead=ID)' lands in edit mode. The full page now edits in place (lead-page-content.tsx:602) and `grep 'leads?lead='` across app/ and components/ returns nothing. Dead handler.

UNUSED reply-draft STATE IN THE LEADS LIST. leads-content.tsx:82-95 declares the ReplyDraft interface and :179 declares `const [selectedReplyDraft, setSelectedReplyDraft] = useState<ReplyDraft|null>(null)`. Neither the value nor the setter is referenced anywhere in the file. The AI-reply feature exists only on the full page.

GET /api/admin/leads/[id] RETURNS A `calls` ARRAY NOBODY READS. leads/[id]/route.ts:84-88 and :105 ship every discovery call for the lead, but both consumers type the response without it (leads-content.tsx:267-271, lead-page-content.tsx:173-178) because <DiscoveryCallsCard> fetches /api/admin/leads/<id>/calls itself. Every lead-detail load pays for a duplicate query.

THREE LEAD/DEAL API ROUTES HAVE NO CALLER AT ALL. /api/admin/leads/bulk-actions (208 lines: archive, rescore, assign_owner, set_status, delete over up to 500 ids) is referenced by no UI and no MCP tool — and the /leads DataTable does not even enable row selection, so the 'I selected 50 leads' flow its doc-comment describes cannot be started. /api/admin/leads/backfill-fields (275 lines) has no caller either. /api/admin/pipeline/seed (48 lines) has no caller and duplicates the auto-seed inside GET /api/admin/pipeline/stages — with a DIFFERENT stage set (Inquiry/Contacted/Discovery/Proposal Sent/Won/Lost/Stalled vs Lead/Discovery/Proposal/Negotiation/Verbal Commit/Stalled/Closed Won/Closed Lost).

TWO MORE ROUTES ARE MCP-ONLY, WITH NO SCREEN. /api/admin/leads/rescore-all (the 'I just tuned the ICP rubric, re-score everything' flow) and /api/admin/leads/triage-pipeline (the 'find deals that should have been leads' flow, which DELETES deals) can only be run from the worker MCP (index.ts:2287, :2075). Neither has a button, a dry-run preview screen, or any surfaced result.

THREE MORE ROUTES ARE FETCHED BY NOTHING IN THE UI. GET /api/admin/deals/[id]/activities is redundant with the main deal GET. GET /api/admin/deals/[id]/nudges returns nudge history that the deal detail never renders — there is a Nudge compose button but no sent/scheduled list, so a scheduled nudge is invisible as well as unsent. GET /api/admin/calls (scheduled_calls) is used only by client-detail and MCP.

THE `call` ACTIVITY TYPE IS UNREACHABLE FROM THE DIALOG. ActivityFormDialog offers note / meeting / email / task (deal-detail.tsx:3096-3101), but the Date + Duration fields are rendered `{(type === 'call' || type === 'meeting') && ...}` (:3187). 'call' can never be selected, so that half of the condition is dead — and the ACTIVITY_ICONS/COLORS maps still carry a `call` entry (:143, :172).

THE STAGE-TIGHTEN GUARD IS KEYED TO STAGES THE FALLBACK SET DOES NOT HAVE. TIGHTEN_AT_STAGE_SLUGS = proposal, negotiation, verbal_commit (deal-detail.tsx:1123), which match the API's seeded defaults. The deals-content DEFAULT_STAGES fallback (:91-99) uses Inquiry / Contacted / Discovery / Proposal Sent / Won / Lost / Stalled — none of which slugify into that set. The comment at :1119-1122 acknowledges the prompt 'will just stop firing' if stages are renamed; on the fallback set it never fires at all.

YOU CANNOT PICK A CLIENT IN THE NEW DEAL DIALOG. `const [orgId] = useState(initialOrgId ?? '')` (deals-content.tsx:1608) is declared with no setter and there is no company field in the form. The only way to attach an org at creation is to arrive via ?new=1&orgId=<id>; otherwise every deal is created unlinked and must be relinked from the detail page's OrgSelector. There is no owner field either, so the owner is always whatever `pipeline.defaultDealOwnerId` resolves to.

THE DEALS VALUE FILTER COMPARES THE WRONG NUMBER. Min/Max Value filter against `d.value` (deals-content.tsx:291-298), the native-currency legacy rollup (upfront + monthly*12), while every displayed figure uses valueNzd through toDisplay. A USD deal is filtered on its USD number and displayed as NZD, so the filter and the column disagree.

CLIENT LTV MIXES CURRENCIES AND LABELS THE RESULT NZD. deals/[id]/route.ts:214 computes total = SUM(invoices.totalUsd) + SUM(deals.valueNzd), and deal-detail.tsx:779 renders it as formatCurrency(ltv.total, 'NZD'). USD invoice totals are added to NZD deal values and the sum is presented as NZD.

THE DEAL BOARD LINKS THROUGH A PERMANENT REDIRECT. Both the kanban card (deals-content.tsx:1256) and the list title (:1497) link to /pipeline/<id>, which next.config.ts:80-81 308-redirects to /deals/<id>. Every deal open costs a round-trip. The back link on the detail page correctly says /deals but is labelled 'Back to Pipeline' (deal-detail.tsx:372, 386).

'CAPACITY IMPACT' AND THE CAPACITY API ONLY UNDERSTAND THE LEGACY HOURS FIELD. /api/admin/pipeline/capacity computes pipelineImpact from estimatedHoursPerWeek alone (capacity/route.ts:94-98), ignoring the newer engagementType / totalHours / hoursPerMonth model that the deal detail's Engagement editor writes. A retainer deal entered as hours/month contributes zero to the forecast. Separately, `currentHoursAllocated` is LOGGED time from timeEntries, not allocated work, so 'utilization' measures the past, not commitment.

THE `mode=score` ENRICH PATH WRITES NO ACTIVITY, SO ITS SCORES ARE INVISIBLE TO THE SPARKLINE. enrich/route.ts:518-543 updates aiScore and lastAiRunAt but stamps nothing on the timeline. ScoreHistorySparkline only reads lead_scored / lead_enriched rows (lead-page-content.tsx:1329). Only the cron (cron/leads-ai/route.ts:262-274) and rescore-all (:195-200) write lead_scored, and only on a CHANGE — so a lead that keeps the same score shows a flat, gap-free history that is not what actually happened.

THE LEAD FULL PAGE SHOWS TWO 'ACTIVITY' HEADINGS. lead-page-content.tsx:868 renders a PageCard titled 'Activity' that contains only the note composer plus, when there is no history, the line 'No activity yet...'; the actual list is a SECOND PageCard titled 'Timeline' at :925. When activities exist the user sees an empty 'Activity' card followed by a 'Timeline' card.
HOT LEADS ROWS DO NOT DEEP-LINK. owner-home.tsx:1112 sends every row's onClick to go('leads') — the list — rather than /leads/<id>. Clicking the top-scored lead loses which one you clicked.

MISCELLANEOUS UNUSED PAYLOAD. GET /api/admin/deals returns notes, closeReason and engagementEndDate that no board or list column renders (deals/route.ts:74-78). GET /api/admin/leads returns archiveReason that nothing renders (leads/route.ts:72). ltv.totalPaidInvoices and ltv.totalWonDeals are returned but only ltv.total, wonDealCount and paidInvoiceCount are used (deal-detail.tsx:775-787). deals-content.tsx:320 keeps `closedDeals` alive with an explicit `void closedDeals // retained for future reuse (was used by avg deal size + win rate)` — two KPIs that were removed from the strip.

The access drawer opens on 'Nothing' with the copy 'The safe start', Save stays disabled until something changes, and a named scope with nobody picked shows a warning instead of silently saving as no access. The design has no tab strip at all and no reportsToId, department or planned-role surface anywhere. The session's decision list explains dropping trackType and two access roles but says nothing about deleting a whole shipped sub-surface. Fix: either bring the tab back or write the decision to retire it so nobody rebuilds it by accident.

THE TWO INERT ACCESS ROLES ARE PRESENTED AS ENFORCED. The 'How a scope reads' legend and the drawer radios describe all three roles in confident present tense ('Does the work: Picks up requests and tasks on the clients they can see'). Per the reader map only project_manager is ever consulted; task_handler and viewer have zero readers. The session's own decision says the two decorative ones would be 'labelled as intent rather than pretending to gate anything' — that labelling is not on the screen. Fix: mark them, e.g. a muted 'not enforced yet' line on those two cards and radios.

TABLET DEAD BAND HIDES LOGIN STATE. @container ops (max-width:68rem) sets .op-cap,.op-login{display:none}; .op-login only comes back at ≤44rem. Verified at 900px: the warning banner still says '2 people cannot sign in — Sam Ellis and Tui Raharuhi' while no row shows Signed in / Invited / No login, and no row shows weekly capacity. The banner points at a column that is not there. Fix: keep .op-login visible at all widths (it is a 100px pill), drop something else.

SKILLS, ROLE AND THE REST OF THE MEMBER RECORD ARE DROPPED. The reader map's table has a skills column (2 chips + '+N') and the form has Skills, Role (Member/Admin), department, reportsToId and roles[]. None of it is here. The only role signal is an 'Owner' pill derived from p.role==='owner', which conflates the workspace admin/member column with the separate teamMemberAccess role — and there is now no way to grant workspace admin at all. Fix: bring skills back on the row (they are how you pick who takes a job) and decide explicitly where admin/member is set.

THE WEEK METER USES A DIFFERENT DENOMINATOR TO THE CAPACITY PAGE. <Slots used={Math.round(p.capacity/8)} total={5} /> hardcodes a 5-day, 40h ceiling. Liam at 32h — a full week for him — renders 4 of 5 filled, reading as 80%. Capacity correctly measures him against his own 32h. Two pages, two denominators for the same person. Fix: drop the slots or scale them to the person's own capacity.

ICON-ONLY DESTRUCTIVE ACTION ON A PHONE. At 375 each row ends with Access, then a bare eye and a bare bin as 44px squares side by side, no labels, no hover to reveal a tooltip. One of them removes a person. The same file already solved this exact problem on Capacity with .ol-flag .ops-iconbtn::after{content:'See the week'}. Fix: apply the same treatment at ≤44rem — 'View as' and 'Remove'.

THE ROLE FILTER IS GONE. The reader map has a nonRemovable role multiselect (Admin / Member). The design has search only. Low cost today at six people, but the filter is what makes the page work at twenty.
THE 'ADD ME' BANNER IS GONE. The live page shows an info banner when the signed-in admin is not on the roster, with an 'Add me' button. Nothing here covers that case.

SMALL: the client checklist inside the Access drawer already scrolls at six clients (max-height 15rem) with no search, and the two explanations of the invalid state — 'Nobody picked yet, so this saves as no access' and the warning Note — both sit below the visible area. Add a search and hoist the warning above the list.
SMALL: Confirm has no Escape handler (Drawer does) and no focus restore on close. Same primitive, two behaviours.

NOTE, NOT A DEFECT: the roster invents four teammates (Maya Chen, Sam Ellis, Priya Nair, Tui Raharuhi). It is stub data and the empty state gets it exactly right ('Just the two of you so far'), but on the one page whose subject is who is in the studio, a six-person roster shapes how the layout is judged. Worth reviewing the six-row and the two-row versions side by side before locking the grid.

THE EIGHT WEEK OUTLOOK DOES NOT SLOPE, WHICH WAS ITS WHOLE POINT. Outlook sets top = max(capacity, booked+pipeline) * 1.08 across all weeks, so with utilisation running 80–113% every column fills 80–100% of its plot. Verified at 1280 in light and dark: eight near-identical teal slabs with a thin gold cap. The only thing that differs is the percentage printed underneath. The stated decision was 'the eight week outlook slopes'; it cannot, by construction, any more than the live version it replaces. Fix: fix the plot ceiling to roughly capacity * 1.4 so a full week fills ~70% and a light week is visibly short, or switch to a deviation-from-ceiling chart with a centre line.

OVER DOES NOT READ AS OVER AT 101–102%. .ol-seg.over is height (total-capacity)/top, so the 102% and 101% weeks get a ~2px red sliver that is invisible against the gold above it. Only the 113% week shows a band. The comment above Outlook claims 'over reads as over at a glance'. Same fix as above: with headroom in the plot, a 2% overshoot becomes a visible 3–4px band, and the ceiling line becomes readable instead of sitting flush against the plot's top border.

THE CAPACITY CEILING LINE IS INDISTINGUISHABLE FROM THE PLOT BORDER. .ol-cap sits at bottom:capacity/top*100%, which is ~92% of the plot height, so on most columns it lands on the container edge. In dark it reads as a highlight rather than a limit. Fix: falls out of the headroom change; also give it a dash or a small end tick so it does not read as chrome.

'CAN WE TAKE THIS ON' ANSWERS WITH A WEEK THAT IS ENDING. firstFree scans D.OUTLOOK from index 0, and index 0 is the current week. Today is Sunday 6 Sep; the answer returned is 'Yes, from the week of 31 Aug' with 'That week has 34h spare'. On a sales call that is a start date you cannot honour. Fix: start the scan at the next full week, or label the current week 'this week, 1 day left' and offer it separately.

THE PERSON DRAWER CONTRADICTS ITS OWN HEADER. Booked reads 44h; 'Where the week went' lists four entries totalling 6.7h, with no 'and N more' and no explanation of the gap. It filters D.ENTRIES by memberId with no week bound and no total. Fix: show the full week and a running total, or state what is shown ('4 entries, 6.7h of 44h logged').

ENTRY TITLES CLIP IN THE DRAWER, THE SAME DEFECT THE SECOND REVIEW PASS FIXED ON THE TRACK BOARDS. In the 30rem drawer .oe-l1 b is nowrap + ellipsis, so rows read 'Mobile nav overlap on iOS...', 'Accessibility pass, contra...', 'Motion timing, reduced m...'. .tk-item-t b already got a two-line clamp for exactly this. Fix: apply the same clamp to .oe-l1 b inside .ops-drawer.

TWO DEAD CONTROLS ON EVERY ROW OF THAT DRAWER. EntryRow is called with ro hardcoded true, so each row carries a greyed pencil and a greyed bin. Fix: omit .oe-a when read only rather than rendering disabled stubs.

THE SECTION HEADER BREAKS AT 375. 'This week, person by person' wraps to two lines while the billable/studio/free swatch legend hangs to its right on the first line, so the title reads as broken around a floating legend. Fix: at ≤44rem drop .ops-sec-r below .ops-sec-t.
CAPACITY HAS NO READ-ONLY HANDLING AT ALL. It never calls useRo. 'Recalculate' and 'Move some work' stay live while viewing as a client. Lower stakes than the Xero drawer but the same inconsistency.

SMALL: 'Free 34h / about 4 days of room' nets Sam's 4h of overtime against other people's idle time. The danger note underneath says the right thing; the KPI on its own reads as more slack than the studio has. Consider 'free where it is free'.

SMALL: the 5 Oct week is the only one over the ceiling and the only one carrying a note ('Staci on leave'). The two facts sit in the same column and the design never joins them. One sentence in the over-ceiling state would.

SIX IDENTICAL SLABS. Every track card is the same four-lane grid with the same four lane headers, so the studio-wide board prints 'UP NEXT / IN THE STUDIO / WITH THE CLIENT / DELIVERED, 30 DAYS' 24 times on one screen, and two adjacent cards both say 'Physitrack' with the only difference in 11px grey ('Large track' vs 'Small track'). This is the same-same card pattern the brief rules out, and at 1280 the page reads as grey-headed repetition rather than a board. Fix: group tracks under one client header (its tracks side by side or stacked inside a single card), and print the lane headers once as a column ruler across the top instead of inside every card.

THE KPIs DO NOT FOLLOW THE FILTER. Chip to Sharesies and the board shows one track while the strip still reads 'Tracks running 6 / Slots open 2 / Queued behind 7 / With the client 2', all computed from the unfiltered tracks array. This is exactly the failure the session's own decision text criticises in the live Time page ('the number in the tile and the number in the table routinely disagree'). Fix: compute the KPIs from shown, or label them 'studio wide' when a client filter is on.

THE EMPTY STATE CONTRADICTS ITSELF. In Empty the Kpis block is guarded by {!empty && ...} but the filter chip row is not, so 'No tracks yet — Tracks come with the Maintain and Scale plans' sits directly under chips reading 'Physitrack 2, Allbirds 2, Sharesies 1, Mahana Orchards 1'. Fix: guard .ops-filters with !empty too.

'SLOT OPEN' MEANS TWO OPPOSITE THINGS. Allbirds' small track shows 'Slot open' with one request queued behind it — a paid slot idle while work waits, the single most expensive state on this page. Mahana Orchards shows the same grey 'Slot open' pill with an empty queue, which is fine. TrackCard renders Pill tone='muted' for both. Fix: a warn-toned 'Idle, 1 waiting' when queue.length > 0 and current is null, and count only those in the 'Slots open' KPI sub-line.

'GIVE IT A TRACK' PROMISES SOMETHING THE PLAN CANNOT DO. In 'Requests with nowhere to sit', SEO audit and fixes is flagged 'Hourly client, no retainer' and still offers 'Give it a track'. There is no track to give. Fix: branch the action on the reason — 'Put them on a plan' for hourly and Tune, 'Give it a track' only when a slot exists.

THE GUARDRAIL IS ON THE WRONG MOVE. Promoting a high-priority item to the top raises a confirm that names both items (good copy: 'This moves Accessibility pass, WCAG AA above Case study template, which the client queued first'). Demoting the client's number one fires immediately and toasts 'Queue reordered. The client sees the new order straight away.' The client-facing harm is on the unguarded side. Fix: confirm any move that changes position 1, in either direction.

THE PRIORITY-BUMP CONFIRM IS NOT REACHABLE IN ONE ACTION. Every 'high' item in D.TRACKS is already at index 0 (tk1 q[0], tk3 q[0]), so the state only appears after you demote an item and re-promote it. It was on the list of states to review; give the demo data one high item sitting at position 2 so it shows on load.
SMALL: 'Queued behind 7 / waiting for a slot' is styled teal — a positive accent on a backlog count. Slate or gold would read truer.

SMALL: at 1280 the queue reorder chevrons are 24px (.tk-move .ops-iconbtn{width:1.5rem}). They are visible at rest, which is right, but 24px is a fiddly desktop target for a reorder you will do repeatedly.

THE CLIENT SEES THE STUDIO'S INTERNAL PRIORITY FLAG. LaneItem renders {item.pri === 'high' && <Pill tone="bad">High</Pill>} with no mine guard, so a red 'High' badge sits on TR-1015 in the client's own 'Up next, your order' lane. Verified in the DOM: one .ops-pill.bad on the portal board. The page's promise directly above it is 'You set the order, we work top down' and 'Move something up any time, no need to ask'. A red priority badge the client did not set says either they did or we override them. Fix: hide pri on the portal, or replace it with something the client owns ('You moved this up').

'WITH THE CLIENT' IS THE LANE NAME THE CLIENT READS. Only the queue lane gets the portal rewrite (.ops-tracks.portal .tk-lane.queue .tk-lane-h span::after{content:', your order'}); Lane title="With the client" is hardcoded. Verified in the DOM: the portal lane headers are 'Up next, your order' / 'In the studio' / 'With the client' / 'Delivered, 30 days'. The empty text underneath gets it right ('Nothing waiting on you') — the header above it does not. Fix: pass the lane titles through the mine flag: 'Waiting on you'.

NO READ-ONLY CUE WHEN AN ADMIN IS PREVIEWING. With the switcher on, every write correctly reports disabled (all six reorder buttons, New request, the ghost-track CTA) but nothing on the page says why. The only explanation is a title tooltip on the buttons that carry roTip, which is a hover-only affordance on desktop and invisible on touch — and TracksClient's New request does not even pass roTip. Fix: an in-surface read-only strip, or at minimum roTip on every gated control.

MEANING IN A ::after. The ', your order' half of the queue lane's label is CSS generated content. It survives most screen readers in Chrome but it cannot be translated, it will not appear in a copy audit, and it is the clause that carries the whole ownership claim. The same pattern is used for 'See the week' on Capacity, where it is genuinely decorative and correctly backed by an aria-label. Here it is not decorative. Fix: put it in the JSX and pass the title through.

SMALL: the empty state subtitle reads 'Your Scale plan runs 2 jobs at once' because tracks is initialised from D.tracksFor regardless of demo. It happens to be true (the plan has two slots, both empty), but confirm that is the intended sentence next to 'Nothing in your tracks yet' rather than a data leak.

SMALL: 'Typical turnaround / 4 days' in the summary strip is hardcoded with no source. On the one strip a client uses to set expectations, say where it comes from (last 30 days, this plan) or drop it.

SMALL: the client can reorder a queue with no guard, including moving something above a job that is already partly done. The studio board asks for confirmation when it reorders on the client's behalf; the client gets none. Probably right, but worth a deliberate decision rather than an asymmetry that fell out.

sales.summary:
Five surfaces, all FIX, none REDO. The thinking behind this area is the best in the prototype: the week grid makes the week the unit and puts money on the surface, the Xero drawer is a thing you read before you run, the access scope is a sentence you can hand to a lawyer, and the plain-words empty states ('Just the two of you so far') are exactly right. Every fix below is local.

Verification: ops.css drives its breakpoints from container queries on the .ops container, so I sized the harness stage to exactly 1280 and 375 CSS px with zoom and walked all five pages in light and dark, plus the drawers, both empty states I could reach, error, and view-as-client. Zero horizontal overflow anywhere. Touch targets all clear 44px at 375 (the search input measures 42.5 inside a 44px wrapper, which is correct). No single-side borders. No em or en dashes.

Three findings would cost real money or real trust:
1. Time. The Xero export drawer is not passed ro. In view-as-client the drawer opens and 'Create 1 draft' reports disabled:false — an admin previewing the portal can raise draft invoices. This contradicts the session's own stated decision.
2. Tracks (client). The internal red 'High' priority pill and the third-person lane name 'With the client' both render on the client's board, on the page whose entire promise is 'you set the order'.
3. Team. There is no Edit action on a person, so weekly capacity — the denominator the whole Capacity page divides by — is uneditable for anyone who already has a login. The Org chart tab, a shipped sub-surface with its own component and API, is deleted with no decision written for it.

Two are self-inflicted repeats of failures this session set out to fix. The Tracks KPI strip keeps studio-wide numbers when a client filter is on, which is the same tile-disagrees-with-table bug the decision text criticises in the live Time page. And the eight-week outlook still cannot slope: Outlook scales every column to the global maximum, so at 80–113% utilisation all eight bars fill 80–100% of their plot and the over-ceiling slice at 101–102% is a 2px sliver. Give the plot headroom (ceiling at ~70% of the plot) and both problems go away.

One precise contrast bug: ops.css .ot-who span{color:var(--text)} also matches the avatar span, so the owner's initials in the running-timer card render at 2.45:1 in light mode. Scope the selector. Separately, .ops-btn.primary is white on --brand (#7AAB6B) at 2.67:1 in both themes — that is inherited from the app-shell tokens and shows up on every primary CTA in the whole prototype, so check it against the shipped app before touching it here.

Taste: the Tracks studio board is the one place the same-same-card rule bites. Six identical four-lane slabs printing the same four lane headers 24 times, with two adjacent cards both titled 'Physitrack'. Group the tracks under one client header and print the lane headers once as a column ruler.

issues: CONTRAST, systemic. The subtle text token is rgb(154,152,143) on light and rgb(107,106,99) on dark, giving 2.54:1 and 2.93:1 where 4.5:1 is required. 48 failing nodes light, 22 dark, and it is carrying real information, not decoration: every column header (.sp-th), every 'company · email' subline, 'Not scored', 'Nothing queued', the 'x promoted or archived leads are hidden' disclosure and the '9 of 11 leads' footer. Fix once at the token, not per page: raise --sp-text-subtle to clear 4.5:1 against both --cream and the dark card surface.

LOADING AND ERROR STATES LIE. Both render resolved KPI numbers (3 / 6 / 1 / 1), resolved chip counts (New 3, Qualifying 4...) and '9 of 11 leads' while the body says 'We could not load your leads' or shows a skeleton. All of that comes off the same single SWR key, so it cannot be known. See leads-error-lt.png and leads-loading-lt.png. Fix: skeleton the band and chip counts with the table, and suppress band, chips, disclosure and footer entirely in the error state (the Calls page already suppresses its digest hero on error, so the pattern exists, it just was not applied consistently).

DARK MODE, row checkboxes render solid white. In leads-ready-dk.png the ten unchecked checkboxes down the left edge are the brightest elements on the page, brighter than the H1. The checkbox keeps a hardcoded white background instead of a surface token. Fix: use the card/input surface var.

375px IS BROKEN, and this is the biggest one. The table-to-cards switch is gated on a JavaScript prop, not on width: sales-pipeline.jsx:58 reads `ctx.isMobile` and there is no matchMedia, no resize listener and no innerWidth anywhere in the module. The container query at `@container sp (max-width:48rem)` correctly handles padding, the band, the toolbar and bottom sheets, but never the table. Result: at a true 375px viewport (leads-375real.png) the desktop table renders with 'aroha@ruruhealth....' and 'hemi@waip...' truncated mid-word and the AI SCORE column clipped off the right edge. Fix: derive isMobile from a container/viewport observer inside the module, or move the card switch into the same container query as everything else.

MOBILE TOUCH TARGETS under the 2.75rem bar. At 390px: the 'Briefing' button, which is the primary action on every mobile lead card, is 40px tall (x9); 'Show them' is 38px; the search input measures 18px. sales-pipeline.css sets `.sp-btn.sm{min-height:2.5rem}` deliberately inside the narrow block. Fix: 2.75rem for .sm too, or stop using .sm for card primaries.

BULK IMPORT COPY IS UNTRUE. Phase 1 says 'Rows are written in batches of 50, and the run keeps going if you close this panel.' Per the reader map the continuation loop is client-driven (up to MAX_LOOPS=50 client POSTs using the server's remainingCsv/remainingMapping). Closing the panel kills the loop. Fix: 'Keep this panel open until it finishes.'

BULK IMPORT PHASE 1 DEAD SPACE. Roughly 470px of empty white between the hint line and the footer (leads-import-lt.png), in a product whose whole thesis is density. Phase 3 (x-import3.png) is excellent by comparison. Fix: make phase 1 a short dialog, or show the nine mappable fields greyed as a preview of what comes next.

NEXT STEP COLUMN IS TOO NARROW FOR ITS OWN CONTENT. Six of nine rows truncate mid-word ('First reply, offer two…', 'Scope the APAC campa…', 'Confirm the Series A ti…'). This is a proposed net-new column, so it has to earn its width. Fix: widen it, or shorten the seeded copy so the column is proven at a realistic width.

TWO READER-MAP COLUMNS DROPPED. The live list has Site (external-link glyph to the website) and Estimate (formatMoney(estimatedValue, currency)); the design has neither. Estimate is money, and the list is where money gets scanned. The detail page still shows 'Estimate NZ$45,000', so the data is there.

PRIVATE MODE IS APPLIED INCONSISTENTLY (x-leads-priv.png). It blurs the PROMOTED count but leaves the other three KPI numbers crisp, leaves 'Worth NZ$42k in the pipeline' crisp directly beneath the blurred one, and leaves the Next step free text crisp even though those strings name client campaigns and funding rounds ('Scope the APAC campa…', 'Confirm the Series A ti…'). Fix: either all four band values carry data-private or none do, and next-step text needs it.
BULK BAR 'Delete' has no danger tone and sits flush beside 'Archive' in identical styling. The underlying route requires payload.confirm === 'DELETE'; the UI should signal that weight.
FILTER ROW 2 is right-aligned, leaving ~700px of empty gutter under the search input at desktop. Fix: left-align it under the search, or fold owner/score/source into the chip row.
SEARCH PLACEHOLDER says 'Search name, company or brief' but emails are displayed on every row and are matched by the query. Add email to the placeholder.

NEXT STEP DUE DATE NEVER BINDS. The date input renders empty (dd/mm/yyyy) while a chip beside it says 'Today' or 'in 3d', and the list column shows the same due date. I verified the DOM: the second input's value is literally ''. Reproduced on 3 of 3 leads I opened (Rachel Kingi, Priya Naidu, and on the deal page for Kowtow). This is the flagship proposal of the whole area, so a half-bound field kills it. Fix: bind the date value; the chip should be derived from it, not parallel to it.

ACTIVITY TIMELINE IS EMPTY ON LEADS THAT PROVABLY HAVE ACTIVITY. Tim Lyons shows 'Nothing logged yet' while the same page says 'Enriched 2d ago · 16,400 tokens spent' and 'Promoted 2d ago' (x-lead-promoted-bottom.png). Aroha Tipene shows it too, though POST /api/admin/leads writes a lead_created activity for every lead. Only Rachel Kingi has a populated timeline. Fix: seed the guaranteed events (lead_created always, lead_enriched/lead_scored whenever enrichedAt is set, lead_promoted whenever promotedDealId is set) so the empty state is only ever reachable when it is true.

PROMOTED BANNER IS BURIED. 'Promoted 2d ago · This lead is now a deal in the pipeline. | Open deal' is the very last element in the right sidebar, after Person, Company, Source and estimate and Brief, on a ~1,600px page. The hero shows only a 'Promoted' status pill. So the single most important fact about the record, and its only route to the deal it became, is a full scroll away. This is the state the designer listed as done. Fix: move it to the hero or directly under it.

BARE UNLABELLED SPARKLINE in the hero, next to the score: a ~78x25px green squiggle with no label, no axis and no value (lead-ready-lt.png, x-lead-promoted2.png). The deal page's own equivalent is labelled 'Estimate history' with a 'Up NZ$4,000 since it was created' chip. Inconsistent with their own treatment, and unlabelled decoration is exactly what the brief rules out. Fix: label it ('84 · 6 pts · min 71 max 88') or drop it.

SIDEBAR IS NOT STICKY and dies ~850px before the left column does. On the 1,987px page the right column ends around y=1,100 and everything below is empty cream (lead-ready-lt-s2.png). Person, Company and Next step are exactly the things you want visible while reading the activity feed. Fix: position:sticky the sidebar.

THREE DIFFERENT REVENUE AND HEADCOUNT NUMBERS ON ONE SCREEN. Company signals says 'Revenue NZ$18m to 24m estimated' and 'Team size 58 to 65 staff'; the Company card 60px to the right says 'Revenue NZ$10m to 25m' and 'Employees 62'; the prose says '60 staff'. Both revenue figures are presented with equal authority and they disagree. Fix: show provenance on the Company card rows, or defer the stored band to the AI signal when both exist.
SEEDED 'Revenue: Global' on the Allbirds lead (x-lead-promoted.png) is not a revenue value.

ACTIVITY ATTRIBUTION IS WRONG. 'Lead captured: Rachel Kingi / Webflow partner directory' is attributed to 'AI · 9d ago'. A Webflow form submission is not AI; per the reader map only lead_enriched and lead_scored are createdById 'system'. Separately, 'Status changed: New to Qualifying' by Liam Miller gets the same gold sparkle icon as the AI rows, so the icon vocabulary stops distinguishing human from system.

LOADING STATE IS SILENT TO ASSISTIVE TECH. Every skeleton block carries aria-hidden='true' and there is no other text, no role='status' and no aria-busy, so the page announces nothing at all while loading. Verified: .sph textContent length is 0. (The visual skeleton itself is a real improvement on the live 'Loading lead...' line.)

NEVER-ENRICHED LEAD: 'Run AI' renders as a secondary outline button identical to Edit, while 'Promote to deal' takes primary. For an unscored lead the highest-value action is Run AI, and the reader map has it primary when never enriched. Also the Next step card renders one field when empty and two when set, so the card changes shape between records.
Score band label ('HOT' / 'WARM') is orphaned right-aligned in the AI briefing card header, detached from the number it describes, which lives up in the hero.
Same contrast token, and same 375px/44px issues as the list.

ERROR STATE KEEPS LIVE COUNTS. calls-error-lt.png shows the triage banner, 'Upcoming 5 / Past 6' and chip counts (Discovery 2, Client check-in 1...) above 'We could not load your calls'. The pre-call digest hero IS correctly suppressed, which proves the pattern was understood and then applied to only one of four elements. Fix: suppress banner, tabs and chips too.

A CANCELLED CALL IS FLAGGED AS A MISSING OUTCOME. On the Past tab (calls-past-lt.png) the Ethique intro call has status Cancelled and its Outcome cell reads 'Not captured' in warning gold. A cancelled call never happened, so there is no outcome to capture and nothing for Liam to fix. Fix: render an em-free neutral dash or 'Cancelled' with no warning tone for cancelled and no_show rows.

GRAMMAR: 'One call needs triage. We could not match it to a lead, deal or client from the attendees. | Show them' — singular subject, plural pronoun. Fix: 'Show it', or make the banner always plural-safe ('N calls need triage … Show them').

ROWS HAVE NO VISIBLE OPEN AFFORDANCE. A Call detail page is the headline addition here, but the table title is plain bold text with no link colour, no underline and no chevron, and the only visible row control is the '...' menu. Meanwhile the hero has an explicit 'Open call' button, so the same action is discoverable in one place and invisible in the other. Fix: style the title as a link or add a trailing chevron.

THE ±60 DAY WINDOW CONTROL IS SPLIT IN TWO. The hint 'Showing the last and next 60 days' sits immediately right of the tabs at x≈240; the 'Last 60 days' select that changes it sits ~900px away at the far right of the filter row. Surfacing the window was the right call; put the sentence and the control together.
TRIAGE BANNER PERSISTS ON THE PAST TAB where the 'Needs triage' chip reads 0, so it points at nothing on the tab you are looking at.
EMPTY STATE CTA ICON: 'Sync calendar' uses a '+' glyph for a refresh action, while the header 'Sync' correctly uses the refresh glyph.

STARTING-SOON HERO TIME drifts with load time. It is seeded as now+24m, so it rendered as 'Today, 7:28 AM' and 'Today, 7:36 AM' across my captures, despite the stated business-hour anchoring applied to the rest of the set. Anchor it too so the prototype never reads as a 7 AM discovery call.
Empty state stacks both tab counts and four 0-count type chips above the leaf empty card, which is a lot of zero chrome (same pattern as Leads and Deals; worth one decision across all three).
Same contrast token and same 375px/44px issues.

BUDGET FIELDS LOSE THEIR CURRENCY. 'Budget from' and 'Budget to' render bare integers, 30000 and 45000, with no currency control, in an app that prints NZ$ on every other money node. The AI suggestion panel directly above the same fields formats the identical numbers as 'NZ$30,000 to NZ$45,000' (x-call-extract.png), so the card contradicts itself within 400px. The reader map's field is multi-currency (NZD/USD/AUD/GBP/EUR) and the record stores budgetCurrency. Fix: restore the currency select and format the values.

OUTCOME CANNOT BE UNSET. The five outcome chips have no cleared state, and saving with an outcome set auto-flips a scheduled call to completed. So a mis-tap on 'No-show' is a one-way door that also changes the call's status. The live control has '- pick after the call -'. Fix: allow deselecting the active chip, or add a 'Not yet' chip.

DISABLED PRIMARY READS AS BROKEN. 'Save call notes' is a dimmed green fill with a check icon when nothing is dirty, which looks like a failed primary rather than 'nothing to save'. Compare 'Map columns' in bulk import, which greys correctly to a secondary. Fix: use the same disabled treatment, or switch the label to 'Saved'.

TWO DECLARED STATES ARE NOT REACHABLE FROM THE HARNESS. The State switcher for this page offers only ready / no-transcript / loading, but the brief claims 'AI extract suggestions', 'action items proposed / created', 'unlinked (triage box)' and 'read-only'. sales.summary:
All six pages: FIX. Nothing needs a REDO, and nothing is ready to ship as-is.

This is the strongest area I have reviewed in this prototype. The density is right, the colour is assigned by meaning rather than sprinkled (money green on value and LTV, growth gold on AI and warnings, time teal on calls and digests, stage tints that survive dark mode), the KPI strips are shared-border bands rather than four floating same-same cards, and leaf radius is genuinely restricted to primary CTAs, icon tiles and hero avatars. The honesty instinct is the best thing about it: "2 promoted or archived leads are hidden by the default filter", "The numbers above cover the 100 loaded, not the whole pipeline", "Without this, the next calendar sync can change it back", "This call is not attached to anything, so it will never show up on a lead or a deal", "A deal without a contact cannot be nudged", "Up to 250,000 characters are stored". The Studio tools menu surfacing three routes that had no UI, with the batch size and the dry-run guarantee written into the sublines, is the single best idea here. Call detail and the Prep/Outcome column swap are real net-new value.

Four defects cut across every page and should be fixed once, centrally, before anything else:

1. Contrast. One subtle-text token fails WCAG AA on both themes (2.54:1 light, 2.93:1 dark against 4.5:1 required) and it is carrying information, not decoration: every column header, every company-email subline, "Nothing queued", "Not scored", the deal cards' close dates and dwell numbers, and the 9px "ACTUAL"/"SET" qualifiers that decision #2 exists to make legible. 48 failing nodes on Leads alone.

2. 375px does not work. The table-to-cards switch is gated on a JavaScript `ctx.isMobile` prop (sales-pipeline.jsx:58, 653, 1015); there is no matchMedia, resize listener or innerWidth in the module. The container query at 48rem correctly handles everything else. At a real 375px viewport all three list pages render the desktop table clipped with mid-word truncated emails. The container-query decision was right; it just was not extended to the one thing that matters most.

3. Loading and error states contradict themselves. Leads, Calls and Deals all render resolved KPI numbers, chip counts and row totals while the body says the data could not load. Calls proves the team knew: its digest hero is correctly suppressed on error while its banner, tabs and chips are not.

4. The Next action / Next step date never binds. The date input renders empty while a due chip beside it, and the list column, both show a value. Verified in the DOM on three leads and one deal. This is the flagship proposal of the area, so a half-wired field undermines the whole argument for adding the column.

Beyond those, the items I would not let through: the dark-mode checkboxes rendering as solid white blocks; the promoted lead's banner and its only route to its deal being buried at the very bottom of a 1,600px page; the Activity timeline reading "Nothing logged yet" on a lead the same page says was enriched 2 days ago for 16,400 tokens; the Auto Nudges toggle being dropped from the one stage it exists for; the estimate-history sparkline being identical on a 75.6k, a 52.6k and a 12k deal; the call detail's budget fields losing their currency 400px below a panel that formats the same numbers as NZ$30,000; and a cancelled call being flagged in warning gold for a missing outcome it could never have.

Two review-coverage gaps worth closing before the next pass: the CallDetail state switcher cannot reach "action items proposed / created" (its only fixture is a lead-linked call, which correctly never gets action items), and the Lead detail switcher cannot deep-link the never-enriched, archived and promoted variants — I had to click through the list to review them.

Screenshots: C:\Users\Work\Projects\tahi-dashboard\.qa-screens\sales-pipeline\ (light, dark, 390 frame, true 375, plus x-* captures of every menu, dialog, drawer and edge-case record).

issues: Flow tiles do not account for the whole list. PROP_FLOW is draft/shared/viewed/accepted/declined (sales-artifacts-data.jsx), so the expired Northwind proposal has no tile: the five tiles read 1+0+2+1+1=5 while the counter next to the search says '6 of 6'. Add expired and withdrawn tiles, or state that the band is a subset.

The 'Sent' tile reads 0 while two proposals are in fact shared. The design promotes a derived 'viewed' status into the same row as stored statuses, so the two shared-and-opened proposals move out of Sent and it shows a hard zero with the filler 'nothing here'. Either nest Viewed under Sent (e.g. '2 sent, both opened') or keep Sent as the count of shared and use Viewed as a separate signal.

Declined tile says 'no figure' while Physitrack sits declined at NZ$3,800/mo. sales-artifacts.jsx:94 sums only D.propValue(p).oneOff. Sum monthly separately and render both, e.g. 'NZ$3,800/mo'. The three filler strings ('no figure', 'nothing here') are also the weakest copy on the surface next to the contracts tiles that say 'not sent' and '2 signatures due'.
Value sub-line has no separator: 'featured Considered', 'accepted Campaign system' (sales-artifacts.jsx:116). Render 'Considered, featured' / 'Campaign system, accepted'.

Every row's sparkline is the same six bars. ReadChip hardcodes Sparkbar values={[3,6,4,9,7,12]}, so a 31-view proposal and a 3-view proposal draw an identical chart. Either derive the bars from the view events or drop the sparkline and keep the number.

'14 views , 4 people' renders with a space on both sides of the comma. .sa-read is a flex row with a 6px column-gap and the comma is its own span, so the gap lands either side of it. Same defect in the schedules Reading column and in both mobile cards. Put the punctuation inside the neighbouring text node, or set gap:0 and use margins.

'Valid until' paints red on decided proposals. Kowtow is Accepted and shows '3 Sep / 3 days ago' in danger red; Physitrack is Declined and shows '15 Aug / 3 weeks ago' in red. Expiry is irrelevant once a proposal is decided: suppress the urgency colour (and probably the whole cell) for accepted/declined/withdrawn.

No column sorting anywhere. The live list (proposals-content.tsx) has sortable Name/Status/Org/Deal/Updated with defaultSort updatedAt desc; the prototype Table has no sort affordance on any of the three lists. For a list Liam will scan daily, at least Value, Valid until and Updated need to sort.

Deal is gone. The live list has a Deal column linking to /pipeline/{dealId}; here the deal appears only inside the builder rail, so you cannot see or filter which pipeline deal a proposal belongs to. The org survives as an avatar in the name cell, which is acceptable; the deal does not survive at all.

Mobile (375) drops the two fields you act on. The card shows title, status, value, views and a relative updated time, but not 'Valid until' and not the owner, and there is no row menu at all, so Open the client view / Draft the contract / Duplicate / Delete are unreachable on a phone. Add a card overflow menu and swap the relative-updated line for the expiry.

At 375 the five flow tiles stack 2-up and fill the entire first screen (about 350px) before the search bar, with a lone Declined tile on its own row. Make the band a horizontally scrollable strip on mobile, or collapse it to a single summary line.

Loading state does not match the loaded layout: the flow band skeleton is one grey slab rather than five tiles and the row skeleton is 4 columns against a 7-column table, so the page jumps on arrival. Mirror the real grid.

Low-severity, worth a decision: each flow tile carries a 1px full-width coloured rule (.sa-flow-rule) hugging its bottom inside edge, inside an all-sides border. It is an element, not a border-bottom, so it passes the letter of the no-single-side-borders rule, but it reads like one. Confirm with Liam.

Blocking, and it repeats on every client-facing cover: the title/accent split produces broken sentences. DocCover and the cover mini-preview do title.replace(orgName,'').trim() then append the org name in green after it, so 'Mahana Orchards ecommerce replatform' renders as 'ecommerce replatform Mahana Orchards' and 'Kowtow Q4 campaign system' as 'Q4 campaign system Kowtow'. The house naming convention puts the client first, so this breaks on essentially every real record. Highlight the org name in place (as composeCoverTitle does live) rather than moving it to the end.

The cover date inputs are hardcoded and contradict the preview directly beneath them. Effective is defaultValue="2026-08-31" and Valid until is defaultValue="2026-09-15" for every proposal, so on the Kowtow deck the form says 15/09/2026 while the 'How it reads' card two inches below says 3 Sep 2026, and on the Sharesies draft it says 15/09/2026 against 6 Oct 2026. Bind both to p.effective / p.expires.

The 'Slide theme' three-way control breaks into two rows at 1280 (verified with the stylesheet's real breakpoints applied): 'Light | Dark' in one segmented group and 'Feature' as a separate selected chip below it. It stops reading as one control. Give the field the full row (wide) or shrink the segment padding.

Field labels are Title Cased by CSS. .sa-field-l sets text-transform:capitalize, so 'Prepared for' renders 'Prepared For', 'Valid until' -> 'Valid Until', 'One off' -> 'One Off', 'Attached schedule' -> 'Attached Schedule', 'Button label' -> 'Button Label'. It fights the sentence-case voice everywhere else and it also hits the client-facing decision modal ('Your Name', 'Anything To Add'). Drop the transform and write the labels as you want them read.

Reading (analytics) numbers the slides 01-08 while the rail numbers the same slides 02-09, because the rail counts the Cover as 01 and the dwell list does not include it. Two numbering systems for the same nine slides on adjacent panels. Number the dwell list to match the rail and add the Cover row (the live viewer already tracks it under the literal 'cover').

A decided proposal is only half locked. The header shows a 'Decided, read only' pill and the editors are disabled, but the rail still offers 'Add a slide' and 'Add a package' because those are gated on ro, not on locked. Gate them on locked too.

'Where this sits' says the artifact you are editing does not exist. spineFor filters proposals with status !== 'draft', so on the Sharesies draft the Proposal step reads 'Not written' while you are standing in it. Same bug on the contract builder ('Not raised' on a draft contract). Pass the current artifact into the spine rather than re-querying.

The accepted builder does not point forward. Decision #8 says accepting a proposal points forward, and the Decisions pane and the list row menu both offer 'Draft the contract' - the accepted builder header does not, it offers 'Email link' on a closed deal. Put 'Draft the contract' in the header for accepted proposals.

Pricing notes are dropped. proposalVariants.pricingNotesHtml exists in the schema and renders in the live public viewer; the variant editor here has Name/Button label/Tagline/One off/Monthly/Currency/Attached schedule/scope lines and no pricing-notes field, and the viewer never renders it. Add it or state the decision to retire the column.

The add-slide picker is undesigned. The live builder offers a grouped picker of ~16 typed slides (Common: overview, value anchor, process, retainer offer, case study, testimonials, founders, partner badges, FAQ, terms; Other: differentiators, guarantee, testimonial, about, shared scope, custom text). Here 'Add a slide' fires a toast. That picker is the most content-heavy decision on the surface and it is the one thing not drawn.
Both decisions on the Kowtow deck are stamped '2:41pm' because D.stampNZ hardcodes the time. On a panel whose whole job is provenance, give the two events different times.

The cancelled Northwind MSA shows '0 of 1' and 'waiting on Unknown'. SignProgress takes signers.filter(status==='pending')[0] and falls through to D.person(undefined), which returns the 'Unknown' placeholder; the one signer on that contract is 'skipped'. A cancelled contract should show no waiting-on line at all, and the name fallback should never surface. Same class of problem on the expired Physitrack SOW, which still says 'waiting on Jonty' as though someone owes you a signature.

The contract type is stated twice in adjacent columns: the name sub-line says 'Kowtow, Statement of work' and the very next column shows a 'SOW' pill. Put the org in the sub-line and let the pill carry the type.

'Sent' is gone as a column. The live list has Sent with defaultSort sentAt desc, which is how you triage what is going stale; here the nudge banner covers one stalled contract and nothing else exposes a sent date. Bring the column back or add it to the name sub-line.
No column sorting, same as the other two lists.
The nudge banner is the strongest element here: named contract, days out, named signer, one real CTA. Worth keeping exactly as is.

Blocking: the Reading panel contradicts itself. AVERAGE READ reads '0s / longest 0s' and TOTAL ATTENTION reads '0s / across every visit' while the Recent visits list immediately below shows 3m 4s and 42s. Contracts in sales-artifacts-data.jsx carry views/viewers/countries but no avgMs/longestMs, and Analytics reads those fields. '1 signatures anchored' in the Audit trail rail item (sales-artifacts.jsx:724). Pluralise. The neighbouring Slots item gets this right ('5 slots unfilled' vs '1 slot is still empty').
VIEWS tile sub-line reads 'last today'. The proposal version reads 'last yesterday', which works; 'last today' is not English. Use 'today' or 'last opened today'.

Every audit event is stamped 9:12am. D.stampNZ(e.at,'9:12am') is hardcoded, so on the Kowtow contract 'Sent for signature' and 'Liam Miller signed' are both 27 Aug 2026, 9:12am, and on the Allbirds contract five events span four days at 9:12am each.
